oracles.claim: For the official NIST round-3 KAT randomness (AES256-CTR-DRBG seeded by the recorded seed), the pinned NTRU-20201016 reference shall reproduce pk, sk, ct and ss byte-for-byte and the ciphertext shall decapsulate to the recorded secret.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §4 p.30 KAT; NTRU-Round3.zip KAT/PQCkemKAT_*.rsp; plans/specs/ntru-round3-20201016-spec.pdf sha256 976120f4
limitations: The KAT DRBG sequence is not interchangeable with an arbitrary SHAKE(seed) tape
A mismatch violates the pinned reference profile, not the NTRU specification by itself
Only the first three records of each response file are embedded; the full files are compared when projects/NTRU/kat is present

controls.positive_control: the recorded fixture reproduces pk/sk/ct/ss and decapsulates to the recorded secret
controls.negative_control: a different DRBG seed produces different bytes

oracles.claim: An honest KeyGen, Encaps and Decaps sequence shall succeed, return the profile ABI lengths, and recover the same 32-byte shared secret.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.11-1.12 pp.16-20; NTRU-Round3.zip Reference_Implementation kem.c
limitations: Success is not an IND-CCA2 or quantum-security result

controls.positive_control: a freshly generated key pair encapsulates and decapsulates
controls.negative_control: a tampered ciphertext is covered by ntru_implicit_rejection_exact

oracles.claim: Two pinned NTRU builds of the same parameter set, hash and encoding shall cross-verify in both directions: A keygen/B encaps/A decaps and B keygen/A encaps/B decaps recover the same secret.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.12 pp.19-20; NIST API contract
limitations: Only the same source revision is vendored, so the lane is a same-source single-implementation check
BoringSSL HRSS uses SHA-256 and is not exchangeable with this SHA3-256 profile

controls.positive_control: both exchange directions recover the same shared secret
controls.negative_control: the pair declares public key and ciphertext exchange before enabling

oracles.claim: The independent model shall recompute r and m from a ciphertext and classify membership: r in the ternary set with r[n-1]=0, and for HPS m in T(weight) with equal +1/-1 counts; a non-member must reach the fallback path.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.11.4 pp.17-18; owcpa.c owcpa_check_r/owcpa_check_m
limitations: Candidate ciphertext mutations do not guarantee a specific recovered (r,m); the model classifies each candidate before any target verdict
HRSS has no message-weight condition beyond S3

claim_variants.claim: For HPS, an accepted ciphertext requires r in {0,1,q-1} with r[n-1]=0 and m in T with exactly weight/2 ones and weight/2 twos.
claim_variants.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.11.4 p.18; owcpa_check_r and owcpa_check_m
limitations: The model reproduces the reference check, not a broader security claim

controls.positive_control: the honest (r,m) passes both membership checks
controls.negative_control: a weight-perturbed m is classified as a membership failure

claim_variants.claim: For HRSS only the r-space membership and the padding contract are defined; the message space is all of S3 and the observed classification is recorded as an implementation observation.
claim_variants.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.11.4 pp.17-18; owcpa.c (CheckM compiled out under NTRU_HRSS)
limitations: No message-weight rule is imposed for HRSS

controls.positive_control: the honest (r,m) passes the r-space check
controls.negative_control: a padding-mutated ciphertext is classified as a failure

controls.positive_control: the honest encapsulation decrypts to a member (r,m)
controls.negative_control: a padding or coefficient mutation is classified before any target verdict

oracles.claim: Under the strict ciphertext-padding policy, flipping any unused high bit of the final ciphertext byte shall set the failure flag and the output shall equal SHA3-256(prf_key||ct) exactly; NTRU-HPS-4096-821 has no unused field and is not applicable.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.11.4 note 2 p.18 ("should" fail on non-zero discarded bits); owcpa_check_ciphertext
limitations: The specification text uses "should"; a profile that does not adopt the strict check is not a normative violation
The fallback formula itself (§1.12.3) is normative once fail is confirmed

controls.positive_control: the unmodified ciphertext recovers the encapsulated secret
controls.negative_control: the exact SHA3-256(prf_key||ct) fallback is computed by an independent SHA3 implementation

oracles.claim: On a ciphertext whose failure is independently confirmed, decapsulation shall output exactly SHA3-256(prf_key||ct), stably across calls, with the same 32-byte public output shape as a valid decapsulation.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.12.3 pp.19-20; NTRU-Round3.zip kem.c crypto_kem_dec
limitations: "Reject or different secret" is not accepted as a substitute for the exact formula
The C return code contract (always 0 for the NIST wrapper) is recorded separately as an API observation

controls.positive_control: the valid ciphertext output is the SHA3-256 of the packed r||m
controls.negative_control: the invalid ciphertext output is compared to the independent SHA3-256(prf_key||ct)

oracles.claim: The final 32 secret-key bytes shall act only through the fallback hash: mutating one prf_key byte changes the invalid-ciphertext output to SHA3-256(new_prf||ct), while a valid ciphertext output is unaffected and restoring the key restores the baseline output.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.12.1 and §1.12.3 pp.19-20; kem.c prf buffer construction
limitations: An accidental output equality is not by itself a key-recovery claim; the exact hash formula is required

controls.positive_control: a valid ciphertext is unaffected by the prf key
controls.negative_control: an invalid ciphertext output tracks the prf key through the independent SHA3 computation

oracles.claim: The independent model shall verify f*fp = 1 mod (3, Phi_n), h*hq = 1 mod (q, Phi_n), and, where the model can derive it, the public relation h = g*f^{-1} mod (q, Phi_n); the sampled f and g satisfy their declared spaces.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.11.1-1.11.2 pp.16-17; reference poly_S3_inv/poly_Rq_inv
limitations: A malformed or unknown secret key has a separate API contract (ntru_sk_malformed)

controls.positive_control: the honest key satisfies both inverse relations
controls.negative_control: a perturbed fp breaks the mod-3 inverse relation

oracles.claim: The independent model codec shall round-trip S3 and Rq0 exactly, pack zero padding, and match the reference decoder on every coefficient including the reconstructed last coefficient and the tail trit groups.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.8 pp.10-12; reference pack3.c/packq.c
limitations: Public key and Sq padding aliases are decoded equivalently and are not forced to reject
Out-of-range S3 byte values are classified by ntru_sk_malformed

controls.positive_control: the model and the compiled reference agree on fixed codec fixtures
controls.negative_control: an S3 group of 243..255 is rejected by the model encoder

oracles.claim: A malformed secret key (out-of-range S3 group, corrupted inverse or hq segment) shall not crash, time out or return an out-of-length secret; rejection is required only when the API promises key-import validation.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.8/§1.11; NIST API wrapper has no secret-key import validation contract
limitations: The NIST API does not mandate rejecting malformed keys; acceptance is reported, not treated as a CCA failure
Out-of-range S3 values are only meaningful for complete 5-trit groups and the tail group

controls.negative_control: each malformed key is a real byte-level change recorded in the trace

oracles.claim: The length-aware adapter wrapper shall reject ciphertext, secret key and public key buffers of length 0, 1, L-1 and L+1 at the adapter layer while the exact profile length enters the fixed-size target API.
oracles.source_reference: Harness common contract §1.4.1; NTRU round-3 spec §1.6 byte lengths p.9
limitations: The fixed-pointer NIST API has no observable input length; short-buffer calls are not part of its conformance surface

controls.positive_control: the exact profile length enters the target
controls.negative_control: every wrong length is rejected at the adapter layer without pointer dereference

oracles.claim: The same CSPRNG tape shall reproduce identical key material and ciphertexts on one build; a different tapet shall produce different key material; an injected failure shall be observable by the RNG control.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.4/§1.10/§1.12; harness common contract §1.4
limitations: Same-tape equality only holds for the same build and call path
The void randombytes API cannot report a failure; the failure is observed through the harness control
All-zero successful randomness is not by itself an algorithm violation

controls.positive_control: two runs under the same tape agree
controls.negative_control: a different tape changes the key material

oracles.claim: Zero-length ciphertext or secret key inputs and an RNG failure shall leave a consistent status and output state; the 32-byte secret buffer shall be fully written on success and no sentinel bytes shall remain.
oracles.source_reference: Harness common contract §1.4.5; NTRU round-3 spec §1.12 output contract
limitations: The allowed failure output state is profile-specific; "must zero" is not assumed for all APIs

controls.positive_control: the honest path returns the full 32-byte secret
controls.negative_control: a poisoned 0xA5 output buffer is distinguished from a successful secret

oracles.claim: For profiles that expose the DPKE decrypt entry point, a confirmed fail shall return (pack_S3(0)||pack_S3(0), 1) without leaking the recovered r||m; the pinned KEM adapter does not expose this API.
limitations: NOT_APPLICABLE for the pinned KEM-only adapter; test-only hooks can still expose intermediate values

controls.positive_control: the valid input returns the packed rm
controls.negative_control: the invalid input is checked against the zero-rm shape

oracles.claim: A deliberately faulted build that skips the membership or padding check or returns the valid secret on failure shall be detected by ntru_dpke_membership, ntru_ct_padding and ntru_implicit_rejection_exact.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.11-1.12; harness fault-injection policy
limitations: Opt-in P2 lane; only the shipped test mutants are exercised

controls.negative_control: each shipped mutant is caught by its designated oracle

oracles.claim: The opt-in timing and resource lane shall complete within its budget while comparing valid and different failure-class decapsulations; no timing conclusion is drawn from the sanitized default binary.
oracles.source_reference: NTRU round-3 spec §1.9 pp.12-16 constant-time discussion; harness common §1.4 timing policy
limitations: Opt-in P2 lane; not part of the default smoke contract
A dedicated non-sanitized binary, CPU pinning, warmup and multiple-comparison correction are required before any conclusion

controls.positive_control: the valid path is measured in the same harness
controls.negative_control: the lane reports not_applicable when the timing binary is absent
